rules.source: Irish Data Protection Act 2018, Section 29 — fixes the national age of digital consent (GDPR Article 8) at 16; a child under Section 29 is defined as under 18 for other child-specific protections in the Act. https://caseguard.com/articles/a-new-legal-framework-for-data-protection-in-ireland/

Irish Data Protection Act 2018 — it is a specific criminal offence for a company or corporate body to process a child's personal data for the purposes of direct marketing, profiling, or micro-targeting; the DPC's "Children Front and Centre" guidance sets out 14 child-specific data-processing principles. https://www.dacbeachcroft.com/en/What-we-think/In-the-Spotlight-Processing-Childrens-Personal-Data-in-Ireland-and-beyond

Irish Data Protection Act 2018 — provides a specific, strengthened right to erasure for children with respect to personal data collected when they were offered an information-society service, going beyond the general GDPR Article 17 right. https://www.dataprotection.ie/sites/default/files/uploads/2023-04/DPC_ChildrensData_ParentalConsent.pdf
Criminal Justice (Offences Relating to Information Systems) Act 2017, section 2 — https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2017/act/11/enacted
rules.retrieved_snippet: Irish Statute Book: section 2 makes it an offence to intentionally access an information system by infringing a security measure without lawful authority or reasonable excuse; sections 3 to 6 cover interference with systems and data, interception and tools; the Act gives effect to Directive 2013/40/EU. Penalties not retrieved; revised consolidation at revisedacts.lawreform.ie.

rules.source: Online Safety and Media Regulation Act 2022 and the Coimisiún na Meán Online Safety Code (final, October 2024) — https://www.fieldfisher.com/en-ie/locations/ireland/ireland-blog/online-safety-code-launched-by-coimisiun-na-mean
rules.retrieved_snippet: Law-firm and press summaries: the final Online Safety Code binds video-sharing platforms headquartered in Ireland, requires terms banning cyberbullying, self-harm and eating-disorder promotion, incitement to hatred or violence, terrorism, CSAM and racism, age assurance for pornography and gratuitous violence, parental controls for under-16s, reporting mechanisms, and fines of up to EUR 20 million (one firm: or 10% of turnover). Not an official source.

rules.source: Prohibition of Incitement to Hatred Act 1989 (remains in force) and Criminal Justice (Hate Offences) Act 2024 — https://www.lawsociety.ie/gazette/top-stories/2025/january/legislation-on-hate-crimes-now-in-force/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Law Society Gazette / press: the 2024 Act, signed in October 2024 and commenced 31 December 2024, creates aggravated forms of existing offences motivated by hatred of protected characteristics; amendments removed the proposed incitement-to-hatred offences, so incitement remains governed by the 1989 Act.
